institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was initially supposed to go to New Zealand for my exchange, but because of the corona situation it got cancelled, and I had to choose something in Europe that my program had agreements with. With the given choises i choose BOKU in Vienna, since it sounded the most interesting to me especially with regards to nature. It also looked like a cool university from what i researched at home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Given the corona situation, with a long period, I still had a great time in Austria and at BOKU.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything I needed to know was in the mails I received from BOKU.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I needed assistance with my Learning Agreement, which went fine. I was initially quite stressed with all the deadlines and stuff, but it was possible to make changes to the LA pretty much during the whole stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The orientation days were good. Also went on a trip to a test farm which was a nice way to meet and talk with some of the other students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Me and my study buddy found some housing relatively easy on
www.wg-gesucht.de
. Don't know if we just got lucky, but it seems to be the main website (some Facebook groups also having a lot) for finding shared flats. Personally I REALLY recommend to find some shared flat if you want to meet Austrians, or just some people who aren't studying the same things as yourself!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The campus is located in a nice area - similar to fancy areas of Copenhagen like Hellerup or Frederiksberg. I lived in district 16 (Ottakring) which I found really nice and close to BOKU (15 mins by bike or bus). Other nice districts I visited would be 14, 15, 16, 9, 8, 7, 6, 4.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A LOT of smaller courses. Not like in Copenhagen with 7.5 ECTS courses. Mostly (2)-3-(4) point courses. Was quite easy to register (and deregister) to the courses, but a bit of a nightmare to make everything fit in a schedule. Luckily it was rather flexible, so could figure everything out when I arrived.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: When you get our student login, you could go into the registration portal and register and look when the courses are held.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. You could write to the teacher responsible if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It went okay. Just had to prioritise with some of the courses I knew I really wanted to take, and find other interesting courses. Luckily BOKU offers many interesting courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't be stressed with the Learning Agreement and courses before you arrive. It it first when you arrive that you can see how the courses fit together in a schedule, and you can practically change every single course you had on your Learning Agreement with something else when you arrive - no problem.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's very different from Copenhagen, and the ECTS don't necessarily reflect how high the workload is. Even though you have a lot more courses at one time YOU DONT GO TO TRADITIONAL EXAMS AT THE END FOR ALL COURSES!  (at least for masters courses). Many courses have active attendance and presentations as the 'exams' along the way.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Varied a lot, but as a bachelor student from KU, I was completely fine on all the masters courses i attended.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Same relaxed relations/communication with the teachers/professors. In some cases more engaging for the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Biodiversity crisis – climate crisis 
Ecology of roots and mycorrhiza I
Ecology of roots and mycorrhiza II
Exploratory data analysis
Field camp I - introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences
First steps with R
Foresights - what future to expect? (Late lessons from early warnings)
Plant and Environment
Soils and Global Change
Statistical Growth Models
Statistics with R
Sustainable land use in developing countries

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Field camp I - introduction to mountain forestry and forest sciences
Very nice start to the semester with a week long trip to a hut in the mountains with other students.

Ecology of Roots and Mycorrhiza I&II
Both quite nice and in depth courses focusing on roots and how important and overlooked they are.

Foresights - what future to expect? (Late lessons from early warnings)
Interesting to get an understanding of what foresights (and generally methods for looking into the future) can and cannot do.

Plant and Environment
Big class, but very good lectures for getting an overall understanding of plant responses to environment.

Exporatory data analysis
Really cool course in R. Great younger teacher who explains everything very well.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Mountain huts were quite expensive to stay in. 

Food is in general same price as DK or cheaper. Beers are cheaper. Wine is A LOT cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a university

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hiking either the Stadtwanderweg(s), or in areas around Vienna (Hohe Wand, Schneeberg), skiing (check the ÖBB app for 'cheap' kombi tickets for train and skiing), biking trips (along the Donau is nice), museums, music.
Remember to visit the Vineyards in Autumn to get some nice Sturm!
The app bergfex has a lot of hiking and biking trips!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Abovementioned.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with other students in shared flats.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outdoor life, dressing nicely up for a classical concert.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't get stressed with the Learning Agreement before arriving - you can change everything if you want to.

If you wanna do sports through the university sports, be ready at the computer when registration starts! Everything fills up very quickly.

Write to the professors/teachers if you have questions with anything regarding courses. Most of them respond quickly and are very helpfull.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in another city and exploring it. Being closer to nice nature, and of course meeting new people and making new friends from all across the world!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Corona

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
